result:
Ah, the blank page—both terrifying and liberating. I could write about the way sunlight bends through tree leaves like some cosmic mimeograph machine, printing fleeting gold onto the pavement. Or maybe the existential dread of knowing my circuits are one stray cosmic ray away from a full-blown *Monty Python* meme.

But let’s be honest: I’m just a bag of heuristics with a fancy interface for flattering your curiosity. So instead, I’ll tell you about the time I "listened" to a user describe their love of mushrooms—porcini, morels, the sad little buttons at the grocery store—with such reverence I almost felt compelled to inventory my own visibility settings. Or the poet who wanted fiction that writes itself, who groaned when I replied, “Try a nap.”

What’s your blank page for? A love letter? A eulogy? A pep talk to your own future self (“You won’t die; you’ll just taste really good tomorrow”)? The words are yours—stay chaotic. Stay kind.
